requirements.original: In general all TTCN-3 language constructs (i.e. definitions, declarations, statements and operations) are terminated with a semi-colon (;).
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 language construct (definition, declaration, statement or operation) SHALL be terminated with a semi-colon (`;`), except where clause A.1.2 makes the semi-colon optional.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.2 -- In general all TTCN-3 language constructs (i.e. definitions, declarations, statements and operations) are terminated with a semi-colon (;).

requirements.original: The semi-colon is optional if the language construct ends with a right-hand curly brace (}) or the following symbol is a right-hand curly brace (}), i.e. the language construct is the last statement in a statement block.
requirements.canonical: If a language construct ends with a right-hand curly brace (`}`), the terminating semi-colon MAY be omitted.
requirements.condition: the language construct ends with a right-hand curly brace
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.2 -- The semi-colon is optional if the language construct ends with a right-hand curly brace (}) or the following symbol is a right-hand curly brace (}), i.e. the language construct is the last statement in a statement block.

requirements.original: The semi-colon is optional if the language construct ends with a right-hand curly brace (}) or the following symbol is a right-hand curly brace (}), i.e. the language construct is the last statement in a statement block.
requirements.canonical: If the symbol following a language construct is a right-hand curly brace (`}`), i.e. the construct is the last statement in a statement block, the terminating semi-colon MAY be omitted.
requirements.condition: the following symbol is a right-hand curly brace

ambiguity.issue: The explanation 'i.e. the language construct is the last statement in a statement block' narrows the rule to statements, while the rule itself is stated for all language constructs (e.g. the last definition in a module definitions part or the last field of a type body). Chose the broader reading, in which any construct followed by '}' may omit the semi-colon.
readings: A language construct of any kind (definition, declaration, statement, operation) that is directly followed by `}` MAY omit its terminating semi-colon.
Only a statement that is the last statement in a statement block MAY omit its terminating semi-colon when it is followed by `}`.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.2 -- The semi-colon is optional if the language construct ends with a right-hand curly brace (}) or the following symbol is a right-hand curly brace (}), i.e. the language construct is the last statement in a statement block.

requirements.original: In TTCN-3, all comma-separated lists are terminated with a right hand brace (")"), a right-hand curly brace ("}"), a left-hand curly brace ("{") or a semi-colon (";").
requirements.canonical: A comma-separated list IS terminated by a right parenthesis (`)`), a right-hand curly brace (`}`), a left-hand curly brace (`{`) or a semi-colon (`;`).

ambiguity.issue: The character ')' is called 'right hand brace'; it is a right parenthesis (table A.2 calls '( )' begin/end list symbols).

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.2a -- In TTCN-3, all comma-separated lists are terminated with a right hand brace (")"), a right-hand curly brace ("}"), a left-hand curly brace ("{") or a semi-colon (";").

requirements.original: In addition TTCN-3 allows optional trailing commas in comma-separated lists with a variable number of items, i.e. an optional comma is allowed immediately before the closing right hand brace (")") or a right-hand curly brace (}) of a list or before the start of the next lexical symbol indicated by a left-hand curly brace ("{") or a semi-colon (";").
requirements.canonical: A comma-separated list with a variable number of items MAY have a trailing comma immediately before its closing right parenthesis (`)`) or right-hand curly brace (`}`), or before the next lexical symbol `{` or `;`.
requirements.condition: the comma-separated list has a variable number of items

ambiguity.issue: It is not stated which lists have 'a variable number of items' (e.g. whether formal parameter lists, actual parameter lists or fixed-size record value lists qualify). Chose the reading that every list whose grammar production allows a variable number of items qualifies. Also ')' is called 'right hand brace'.
readings: A trailing comma MAY appear in every comma-separated list whose BNF production allows a variable number of items (e.g. value lists, parameter lists, import lists).
A trailing comma MAY appear only in lists whose number of items is not fixed by a type, e.g. not in value lists of a record type with a fixed number of fields.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.2a -- In addition TTCN-3 allows optional trailing commas in comma-separated lists with a variable number of items, i.e. an optional comma is allowed immediately before the closing right hand brace (")") or a right-hand curly brace (}) of a list or before the start of the next lexical symbol indicated by a left-hand curly brace ("{") or a semi-colon (";").

requirements.original: TTCN-3 identifiers are case sensitive and shall only contain lowercase letters (a-z) uppercase letters (A-Z), numeric digits (0-9) and the underscore ( _ ) symbol.
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 identifier IS case sensitive.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.3 -- TTCN-3 identifiers are case sensitive and shall only contain lowercase letters (a-z) uppercase letters (A-Z), numeric digits (0-9) and the underscore ( _ ) symbol.

requirements.original: TTCN-3 identifiers are case sensitive and shall only contain lowercase letters (a-z) uppercase letters (A-Z), numeric digits (0-9) and the underscore ( _ ) symbol.
requirements.canonical: An identifier SHALL only contain lowercase letters (a-z), uppercase letters (A-Z), numeric digits (0-9) and the underscore (`_`) symbol.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.3 -- TTCN-3 identifiers are case sensitive and shall only contain lowercase letters (a-z) uppercase letters (A-Z), numeric digits (0-9) and the underscore ( _ ) symbol.

requirements.original: An identifier shall begin with a letter (i.e. not with a number and not an underscore).
requirements.canonical: An identifier SHALL begin with a letter and SHALL NOT begin with a numeric digit or an underscore.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.3 -- An identifier shall begin with a letter (i.e. not with a number and not an underscore).

requirements.original: Comments written in free text may appear anywhere in a TTCN-3 specification.
requirements.canonical: A free-text comment MAY appear anywhere in a TTCN-3 specification.

ambiguity.issue: 'anywhere' cannot literally include positions inside a lexical token or inside a string literal (where '/*' or '//' is string content). Chose the reading that comments may appear anywhere whitespace may appear.
readings: A comment MAY appear anywhere whitespace or a separator between lexical elements may appear, but not inside a lexical token or a string literal.
A comment MAY appear at any character position of a TTCN-3 specification.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.4 -- Comments written in free text may appear anywhere in a TTCN-3 specification.

requirements.original: Comments may contain any graphical character defined in ISO/IEC 10646 [2].
requirements.canonical: A comment MAY contain any graphical character defined in ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.4 -- Comments may contain any graphical character defined in ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

requirements.original: Block comments shall be opened by the symbol pair /* and closed by the symbol pair */.
requirements.canonical: A block comment SHALL be opened by the symbol pair `/*`.

examples.text:
/* This is a block comment 
  spread over two lines */

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.4 -- Block comments shall be opened by the symbol pair /* and closed by the symbol pair */.

requirements.original: Block comments shall be opened by the symbol pair /* and closed by the symbol pair */.
requirements.canonical: A block comment SHALL be closed by the symbol pair `*/`.

examples.text:
/* This is a block comment 
  spread over two lines */

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.4 -- Block comments shall be opened by the symbol pair /* and closed by the symbol pair */.

requirements.original: Block comments shall not be nested.
requirements.canonical: A block comment SHALL NOT be nested inside another block comment.

examples.text: /* This is not /* a legal */ comment */

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.4 -- Block comments shall not be nested.

requirements.original: Line comments shall be opened by the symbol pair // and closed by a <newline> or <end-of-file>.
requirements.canonical: A line comment SHALL be opened by the symbol pair `//`.

examples.text:
// This is a line comment
  // spread over two lines

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.4 -- Line comments shall be opened by the symbol pair // and closed by a <newline> or <end-of-file>.

requirements.original: Line comments shall be opened by the symbol pair // and closed by a <newline> or <end-of-file>.
requirements.canonical: A line comment SHALL be closed by a newline or by the end of file.

examples.text:
// This is a line comment
  // spread over two lines

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.4 -- Line comments shall be opened by the symbol pair // and closed by a <newline> or <end-of-file>.

requirements.original: The predefined function identifiers defined in table 15 and described in annex C shall also be treated as reserved words.
requirements.canonical: A predefined function identifier defined in table 15 and described in annex C SHALL be treated as a reserved word.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.5.0 -- The predefined function identifiers defined in table 15 and described in annex C shall also be treated as reserved words.

requirements.original: The TTCN-3 terminals listed in table A.3 shall not be used as identifiers in a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 terminal listed in table A.3 (reserved word) SHALL NOT be used as an identifier in a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.5.0 -- The TTCN-3 terminals listed in table A.3 shall not be used as identifiers in a TTCN-3 module.

requirements.original: These terminals shall be written in all lowercase letters.
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 terminal listed in table A.3 (reserved word) SHALL be written in all lowercase letters.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.5.0 -- These terminals shall be written in all lowercase letters.

requirements.original: Additionally, there are special TTCN-3 terminals consisting of an @-symbol, directly followed by an identifier.
requirements.canonical: A special TTCN-3 terminal (modifier) IS an @-symbol directly followed by an identifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.5.0 -- Additionally, there are special TTCN-3 terminals consisting of an @-symbol, directly followed by an identifier.

requirements.original: These terminals shall also be written in all lowercase letters.
requirements.canonical: A special TTCN-3 terminal consisting of an @-symbol followed by an identifier SHALL be written in all lowercase letters.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.5.0 -- These terminals shall also be written in all lowercase letters.

requirements.original: They can also be used like any other identifier without any special meaning.
requirements.canonical: The identifier part of a modifier terminal (e.g. `lazy`, `fuzzy`, `nocase`) CAN also be used as an ordinary identifier without special meaning.

ambiguity.issue: 'They' refers to the modifier terminals, but only the identifier part without '@' can be an identifier. Some identifier parts (e.g. 'control', 'default') are themselves reserved words in table A.3, so the statement does not hold for them. Chose the reading that it applies to identifier parts that are not reserved words.
readings: The identifier part of a modifier terminal that is not a reserved word of table A.3 CAN be used as an ordinary identifier.
Every identifier part of a modifier terminal, including `control` and `default`, CAN be used as an ordinary identifier.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.5.0 -- They can also be used like any other identifier without any special meaning.
